Resistance Endogenous friction 09 / 15

Temporal Distance

The gap between when one side is ready and the other is available.

What it looks like Illustrative scenario

Two five-axis machining centres sit idle sixteen hours a day. Sixty kilometres away a robotics integrator needs exactly that capacity, but needs it this week, and the shop's window opens next week. Neither side says so aloud, and idle hours cannot be stored.

Scenario: The Idle Shift

How an AI intervention works AI Memory · AI Matching

Capacity for a service is consumed at delivery and cannot be stockpiled, so the only bridge across time is a market that remembers. Memory holds intent: the integrator's requirement stays live after the first search fails, and the platform reconnects the two the moment the shop's window opens, without either having to search again. Semantic matching keeps the search running at all hours through agents that represent each side, so a deal progresses while its principals are asleep or on the floor.

How traditional markets cope

  • Storage and inventoryuntil the good is a service that cannot be stockpiled
  • Forward contracts and futuresuntil nobody will write one for a one-off job
  • Market makers holding stockuntil no maker will carry a unique item

What's new here

CRM tools track stages; none revives a stalled deal when the market changes. A memory that re-engages both parties once a new carrier or window removes the old blocker is planned.
